circumstances: The researcher closes the submission loop and then returns to the previously parked replication study. Instead of immediately rerunning it, they inspect the reference paper, old preprocessing notes, and the local replication code. They discover that the reference paper's preprocessing description is underspecified in the paper but a supplementary artifact contains enough information to reproduce one missing normalization step. The researcher updates the replication preprocessing code and runs a small sanity check, but does not launch the full replication yet. The afternoon shifts toward deciding whether the replication is still scientifically useful given the manuscript's narrower contribution. Some literature browsing is exploratory, and an unrelated personal task interrupts the evening.

activities.title: Resolve the replication preprocessing blocker
activities.summary: The researcher revisited the old preprocessing discrepancy, inspected the reference paper and supplementary material, found enough information to identify a missing normalization step, implemented it locally, passed preprocessing checks and a smoke test, and documented the remaining questions.

label_notes.context: First substantive return to the replication study after it was parked for several days.

activities.title: Evaluate whether the replication study is still worth running
activities.summary: The researcher read later work citing the reference method, considered the limitations of the replication, wrote explicit resume/pause/abandon criteria, captured possible follow-up questions, and revised the plan toward one bounded replication run rather than a broad extension.

activities.title: Finalize bounded replication plan and rank future questions
activities.summary: After a short personal delivery-related search, the researcher finalized a stopping condition for one full replication run and ranked possible follow-up questions while explicitly deferring a broad benchmark search.

label_notes.context: Closing the decision loop without committing to a large new project.

key_observations: The manuscript submission loop was closed and the exact submitted state was archived.
The previously blocking replication preprocessing issue was partially resolved using supplementary information from the reference work.
The replication is now technically runnable, but its scientific value is less obvious than it was before the main manuscript narrowed its contribution.
Rather than launching a broad replication or benchmark sweep, the researcher defined one bounded full run with an explicit stopping condition.
Several possible next research questions were captured, but broad exploration was deliberately deferred.
priority_alignment: The researcher completed the final submission administration before switching projects.
